items.title: SA government plans to ban ticketless parking fines

children.content: The state government says it will introduce regulation making it mandatory for council inspectors to leave a physical ticket on the car or hand it to the driver.

items.title: 94yo poet who can't read or write celebrated in Stockman's Hall of Fame

children.content: Jim O'Connor never learned to read or write, but he forged a life learning from the outback to become a stockman, poet and legend.

image.altText: Jim looks at the camera while holding a tyre upwrite beside his car.

items.title: Residents demand traffic fix for 'horrendous' SA road

children.content: Residents in Adelaide's fastest-growing council area are calling on the government to fix a litany of traffic flow problems, in a region where 10 people per day are projected to move in over the next 20 years.

image.altText: A column of traffic banked up on a suburban road.

items.title: Spectacular cave site "neglected" after five years closed to tourists

children.content: Princess Margaret Rose Cave has been a popular tourist destination for generations, but the public hasn't been inside since 2021. Millions are being spent on upgrades, but the site's reopening has been repeatedly delayed.

items.title: Man arrested and charged for alleged harassment of SA Speaker

children.content: South Australian Police have arrested and charged a man for alleged stalking and harassment.

image.altText: A man with a short cropped haircut, wearing large sunglasses and a red sports hoodie, standing in front of a fence and gum tree

items.title: Cooking classes help cut cost of living and boost social connection

children.content: A regional community centre's free weekly cooking class, using homegrown and donated ingredients, is teaching people to cook on a budget, while fostering connections.

image.altText: A smiling woman wears glasses and holds a knife while cutting up some carrots on a chopping board in an outside kitchen.

items.title: Anger over Tungkillo data centre should have Labor on red alert

children.content: With the Liberals, One Nation and the Greens all leaning into community fears about data centres, the Malinauskas government could be left holding the bag if it can't regulate them properly.

image.altText: A community protest event against a data centre.

items.title: Indigenous people 'very rarely' sit on a jury in SA, report finds

children.content: Despite being over-represented in the criminal justice system, a report has found Indigenous people are not given equal opportunity to serve on juries.

image.altText: indigenous jurors

items.title: Threatening, sexist messages scrawled on balloons left at MP's office

children.content: Threatening, sexist and abusive messages scrawled on balloons have been left outside the suburban electorate office of South Australian government MP Jayne Stinson, with police confirming they are investigating the matter.

image.altText: Balloons with abusive messages that were left outside an electorate office.

items.title: Young victim of hotel fall died in 'tragic' accident, parents say

children.content: The grief-stricken parents of Natasha Lawton, who died in a fall at a Hindley Street hotel in Adelaide's CBD, have described their daughter as someone who "loved life and lived every minute".

image.altText: A portrait of Natasha Lawton, who later died in a tragic accident.

items.title: Baseballer loses sight in one eye in 'horrific freak accident'

children.content: An Adelaide club baseballer struck by a ball in an "horrific freak accident" during a weekend game has permanently lose sight in his right eye, his close friend and former teammate says.

image.altText: A group of Adelaide baseballers.

items.title: A Batmobile, Wharfie Time and an elephant — the footy gimmicks gone wrong

children.content: Forget Wharfie Time. Australian Rules football has a long history of gimmicks that haven't always turned out well, and they have involved everything from a hovercraft to a Batmobile and even an elephant.

image.altText: A colourful screen with the words Wharfie Time showing

items.title: Brothers open Ceduna's first barber shop in 50 years

children.content: Two Eyre Peninsula brothers have opened a 100 per cent Aboriginal-owned barber shop in the main street of Ceduna, the first men's hairdresser in the town for 50 years.

desktop.altText: Tha Bruthaz Barbershop had humble beginnings in the family shed.

items.title: Women's pelvic health surgeon among SA's Australian of the Year winners

children.content: An endo-gynaecologist specialising in pelvic floor treatments has been named the South Australia's 2027 Australian of the Year in a ceremony where the former recipient doubled down on her wish to secure a spot on a future space mission.

image.altText: A woman being presented with an award by another woman.

items.title: LIV Golf to wind down after five years of rebel league

children.content: LIV Golf is closing down after losing the financial support it had hoped to secure from BC Partners to keep the league afloat.

image.altText: Golfer hits a tee shot with an iron in front of a packed grandstand

items.title: Once-green SA landscape now 'barren' in efforts to stop pest

children.content: An invasive sap-sucking insect that kills pines has led to the removal of more than 5,000 trees across Adelaide's north-east, with residents lamenting the loss of the area's charm.

image.altText: Image of a hill cleared of pine trees with people walking along the crest

items.title: Pilot died while trying to avoid power pole, final report finds

children.content: A final report into a plane crash on the Lower Eyre Peninsula that killed pilot Jarred Wait found he died while trying to avoid a power pole during wheat spraying.

image.altText: A bald man, smiling, in a chequered shirt.

items.title: Six childcare centres to close in SA after failing to find buyer

children.content: Six Edge Early Learning centres will permanently close across South Australia tomorrow, leaving families scrambling at short-notice to find alternative care for their children.

image.altText: A green and black sign on a modern building saying EDGE EARLY LEARNING

items.title: Bandicoot research uncovers new subspecies amid conservation calls

children.content: Researchers say new discoveries about bandicoot species could have conservation implications for South Australian populations of the marsupials.

image.altText: A close-up of a baby bandicoot, held in the palm of a human hand.

items.title: Prime minister scuttles plans to sell off Defence sites despite audit

children.content: The prime minister vows to keep Victoria Barracks in Sydney in public hands, following widespread backlash over plans for the heritage-listed site to be sold off.

image.altText: Anthony Albanese and Richard Marles give a press conference.

items.title: The life of 'Russian starvation and torture' Ukrainians finally escaped

children.content: In Russian-controlled Oleshky, Ukrainians say they were forcibly starved and tortured before an evacuation mission allowed them to flee.

image.altText: An emotional man hugging another person draped in a blue and yellow Ukrainian flag, surrounded by groups of people.

items.title: Explosions in Strait of Hormuz as Iran reviews de-escalation proposals

children.content: Explosions are heard on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, and tankers in the strategic waterway catch fire after hitting mines. Meanwhile, Iran says it has lifted a 2,000km limit on the range of its missiles.

image.altText: Boats anchored on a waterway, seen from a shaley coast.

children.content: A cold front brought rain and storms, and saw temperatures drop by as much as 10 degrees Celsius in some Sydney suburbs.
